name: Kings Peak and South Kings Peak

legs.connect: Drop off Kings and follow the crest south for roughly three quarters of a mile of talus, then retrace it, since there is no easier way off.

duration: 1 long day from camp; 2–3 days in all
how: Most parties climb Kings first, via Anderson Pass and its talus north ridge, then walk the connecting crest to the slightly lower South Kings. The extra summit is modest: a couple of miles out and back with around a thousand feet of up and down, all on boulders. Climbers often add Henrys Fork Peak from the same pass, and strong parties string on Trail Rider, Painter and more along the crest.
descent: Return along the ridge to Anderson Pass, then go back over Gunsight Pass (the cutoff below the pass saves a couple of miles) and down the Henrys Fork trail.
logistics: Usual base is Dollar Lake, about 8 miles in from the Henrys Fork trailhead; some start from the Yellowstone side instead. Go early, as afternoon storms and squalls are a recurring problem on the ridge.
notes: Classes from the ridge-run report: Kings 1+, South Kings 2, Henrys Fork Peak 2. Outdoor-click report plans Kings, South Kings and Dome as one summit day from Dollar Lake; the 0.75 mile gap is from the second page. Other reports read (14ers.com, valhikes, wildernessbeta, yonderlust) climbed Kings alone. SummitPost logs 403 (search snippets only, not used).

name: Granite Peak and Tempest Mountain

legs.connect: Descend the boulder slopes on Tempest's far side to the saddle at about 11,550 ft, then scramble the south side of the saddle to the start of the technical ground.

duration: 2 days, or a very long single day
how: The approach crosses the Froze-to-Death Plateau, and the way to Granite runs over or around Tempest to the low saddle between them, so Tempest is the natural warm-up or afternoon add-on. Beyond the saddle a third-class scramble leads to about 12,300 ft, where exposed climbing of low fifth class begins; many parties rope up and rappel it. Tempest itself is an easy walk from the saddle.
descent: Rappel or downclimb the technical section, return to the saddle, then climb back to the plateau and walk to camp or out to the lake.
logistics: Most parties camp on or near the plateau or at the saddle, where water is scarce, and a few do it in one 16 to 21 hour day from Mystic Lake. Start early, since afternoon thunderstorms are common and the plateau is exposed.
notes: Granite crux grade disagrees: IV 5.4 vs low 5th vs 4+/5.4-5.5 (14ers.com report 4763 read); higher kept as low fifth class. Leg route names come from the first source only. Reports differ on whether Tempest is summited on the same trip: one party added it from the saddle, one climbed only Tempest from the plateau, one passed it. Moderate evidence of commonality only.
